Students admitted to ASU under the Western Undergraduate Exchange, or WUE, program in spring 2026 or earlier will continue to receive the WUE tuition rate for the duration of their undergraduate program, provided they maintain continuous enrollment and meet renewal criteria.
The ASU Commitment Scholarship is a new scholarship designed for nonresident students to make an ASU degree more accessible to students nationwide.
Open to first-year, out-of-state (not Arizona) U.S. citizens, regardless of their state of residency, campus choice, or major.
This scholarship is renewable.
Available to out-of-state students enrolled in any degree program on the Phoenix-area campuses, as well as the ASU California Center in Los Angeles.
It can be combined with the New American University Scholarship.
Out-of-state transfer students can be automatically considered for a New American University Scholarship upon admission with a minimum 3.0 cumulative transfer GPA.
Scholarship amounts vary based on GPA.
ASU will no longer participate in the WUE program starting with students admitted for fall 2026.
The ASU Commitment Scholarship ensures nonresident students have access to a high-quality education at a great value, wherever they begin their ASU journey.

Students who have earned an Associate of Applied Science degree from a regionally accredited Arizona community college may be eligible to transfer up to 75 credits toward the Bachelor of Applied Science degree.
Students pursuing the 75 credit option may have more than 45 credit hours to complete their BAS upon transfer to ASU.
